author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: The Internet
summary: The Internet grew from early research on packet switching and the ARPANET. On January 1, 1983, ARPANET hosts moved from the NCP protocol to TCP/IP in a flag-day transition that required all hosts to convert at once. At its official 1983 launch, the Internet was a modest experimental network of networks owned by the U.S. government. Commercial and worldwide growth came later.

uncertainty.note: January 1, 1983 was the coordinated Flag Day cutover date when TCP/IP became the standard host protocol on ARPANET.

where.modern_name: Worldwide; stand-in pin at Arlington, Virginia, United States

importance.justification: The adoption of TCP/IP created the universal digital communications backbone interconnecting global commerce, communication, and human society.

related.because: Packet switching pioneered on ARPANET provided the underlying network infrastructure upgraded to TCP/IP.
The standardized IP internetwork enabled Tim Berners-Lee to develop and deploy the World Wide Web as an application layer protocol.
